Praise be to Jesus the Messiah, to our Lord who is with us, who walks with us. Giving thanks to Mother at Kreupasanam who tells us not to be sad no matter what trouble comes.
And to the Holy Spirit who guides us, we continue our testimony.
My name is Nitha, this is my husband Binoy, this is my daughter Eva, and we are coming from Canada, we arrived yesterday morning.
We are staying here for three days, we haven't even gone home, we came straight here because this is like a dream land for us.
For the past nine months we longed to come here as soon as possible and give our testimony, and by the plan of Jesus and Mother we are standing on this platform today, for which we are very grateful.
For four months doctors said his leg must be amputated, yet we travelled from Canada yesterday and are standing here today.
First he was in a wheelchair, then a walker, then a cane, and now he is walking and standing on this stage through the powerful presence of Mother the Pilgrim Mother in our life.
That is our testimony, these nine months of our life are our testimony, and though I don’t know if I can say it quickly, I will try.
From this January he had diabetes but no complications, and suddenly he got severe osteomyelitis, a serious bone infection.
By the time we reached the hospital, Binoy’s blood and body,
Almost everything was infected; the whole leg was almost fully infected, and the MRI showed infection everywhere.
During that time of infection, one of our friends told me, “Sister, put a Candle Light Prayer,” but at that time I had no faith in Kreupasanam Mother or anything.
But when that child insisted so much, I thought there must be something in it, and believing that, I did the Candle Light Prayer.
Before that I must say something: after putting Binoy into the car, I remembered a paper my cousin had given me last year from Kreupasanam.
But because I had no faith, I had never even read it; I had kept it inside some shelf.
As I was getting into the car, I felt as if someone was telling me, “Daughter, take that paper, take that paper.” I ran and opened the shelf,
and in the exact shelf I opened, the paper was there; for one year I had never touched or read it, but I took it.
I went to the hospital and we were lying in the emergency; the Canadian medical system is not like here, it is very, very difficult.
For four days we were simply lying in the emergency in a wheelchair.
At that time, even though I didn’t have faith, I kept that paper near Binoy’s leg.
On the second day the doctor came and said, “We need to do surgery tomorrow; we are going to cut and removing some flesh out,” and they told me all this.
That is when I remembered what that child told me, and I looked up the Candle Light Prayer website.
I wrote something there, surrendering Binoy’s leg and everything, and I placed the Candle Light Prayer.
After some time the surgeon came back, tapped on my shoulder, and told me, “Because of you, we are not doing any surgery tomorrow.”
We were shocked and couldn’t understand what was happening.
After that we started another treatment, and the treatment began.
We stayed in the hospital for almost two weeks, and during that time we went through many difficulties because Binoy would not agree to any procedure.
All our friends were bringing this blessed salt and honey remedy, and though I didn’t really believe in it, I gave it to him thinking, “They are giving it with care.” After that,
the treatment there was extremely delayed, and we could not move him to another hospital as we wished, and we were going forward through very difficult circumstances.
After two weeks, by Mother’s intervention, we received many treatments—if I start explaining, there is a lot to say, so I am keeping it short.
Mother enabled us to get many treatments, and we reached home, and after one week of reaching home, my cousin said, “Sister, pray the Apparition Prayer.” I told her,
“Daughter, I don’t have faith; I won’t do it.” After one week,
a family whom Mother had sent came to our house and shared their experiences, but they never told us to take the Covenant.
They left, and after they left, I heard a word from Binoy’s mouth: “I also want to give testimony.” Our cousin was downstairs,
and she said, “Brother, without taking the Covenant, you won’t be able to do that.” Then I told this girl,
“Please show me how to take it online.” She showed me,
and I took Binoy, made him lie down, and I was looking at the face of Jesus not knowing what would happen in our life or how it would move forward.
Amputation was the final decision the doctors had given, and we were completely shattered at that time.
As I was looking at Jesus’ face, I felt Mother telling me in my ear, “Daughter, just try taking this Covenant online.” I opened it,
and when I looked at it, every requirement written there was something I could not do because my life was not like that, our life was not like that.
I switched it on and within one and a half hours I took the Covenant; I had never heard of or seen such things happening in just one and a half hours, and I did not even know what this place was.
I had never seen even a single picture of this Mother, I knew nothing, but I took the Covenant in just one and a half hours while looking at the face of Jesus.
After taking the Covenant, when I went near Binoy to tell him, it had been one and a half months since he had slept even for a night—day and night he couldn’t sleep due to tension and severe irritation.
When I took the Covenant and came into the room, Binoy was lying peacefully and sleeping, and for the first time in one and a half months, I also slept peacefully.
The next day Binoy told me, “Yesterday I slept very well,” and that is when I told him, “I took the Covenant yesterday,” and that is when Binoy came to know.
From that day onward, Mother began taking our life to another level.
After that, on the second or third day, the doctor called and said Binoy’s hemoglobin was extremely low, and again I became weak and sat down like this.
Mass was going online at that time, and as I was sitting there, a strong smell was coming from the rosary.
I had never heard any testimonies before, so I didn’t know anything about the fragrance, but I could smell it, and that was the first time Mother intervened in my life—through the fragrance coming from the rosary.
After that, during the first week of taking the Covenant, our life was extremely difficult—hemoglobin kept dropping, and the next day we got an appointment with the angioplasty surgeon.
That Friday, fluid was found in Binoy’s lungs; truly it was a season of trials, and at that time I wasn’t listening to sermons or Father’s talks, only small testimonies.
After that, I started praying a lot.
Then we went for angioplasty, but before that I need to say something—what people say about the Pilgrim Mother coming, I feel it is true.
On the day the hemoglobin dropped, we went to the emergency and after the blood transfusion, my daughter, who has asthma, had some homeopathic medicines we brought from Kerala.
When I came back from the emergency, on our table the rosary was lying there.
To be honest, this rosary is blue in color, and it really looks like Mother.
It was lying on the table, and I wondered where this rosary came from, so I took it and kept it in the place where we keep the rosaries.
After two days, through Mother, for the first time I received this medal into my hand; this medal is just an ordinary medal.
We did not have Covenant medal, and from the day we received it, I began to gain strength.
Truly speaking, from that day I stopped crying and became very strong, and I had no more sadness or distress after receiving it.
On the day I received it, when I tried to quickly put the medal on Binoy’s neck, this rosary caught my eye.
I thought it was the rosary my mother had given me—you know, it is blue and white in color—so I assumed it was hers.
I called my mother and said, “Mom, I put the locket on the rosary you gave me,” and Mom said, “I never gave you such a rosary.”
Then I thought maybe my elder brother gave it, but when I checked, it wasn’t from him either; even today we don’t know where this rosary came from.
This rosary is still blue and white in color, truly like Mother’s color, and it remains the same even now.
After that, during angioplasty they identified a block in Binoy’s leg, and on the day of the angioplasty we reached the hospital.
No one accompanied us who said they would come with us, but Mother gave us a room, and when I entered that room everything was gray—the curtains and even the clock.
There were no religious pictures or anything, that hospital is like that, and we went inside.
The doctor told me Binoy had complications—very low hemoglobin, and fluid collected in his lungs.
After angioplasty he must lie straight for five hours, and we clearly knew that in Binoy’s condition this would not be possible.
Knowing the complications, we still took the risk and admitted him, and at that time we asked the nurse whether we could take the rosary inside.
In Canada that is usually not allowed, but the nurse said, “We can try,” And usually I was someone who couldn’t pray even for half an hour, yet that day,
I sat inside that room for nearly four hours praying to Mother, watching the Mass from here, and calling out to her.
For three to four hours I prayed continuously, with the conviction that Jesus and Mother were right beside me.
After angioplasty, the doctor called me and said there were four blocks, and they cleared them, but many complications were happening inside.
Mother did not allow me to know any of this; I was just alone, and even when it was time for Binoy to come out, he did not come.
When he finally came, he told me there were many complications, and more than that, inside the operation theatre— there was a young Muslim boy who asked Binoy,
“Do you want this rosary in your hand?” And the doctor said one thing: “I know this is your strength,”
and he placed the rosary inside Binoy’s hand and wrapped the bedsheet around it.
He tied it so that when anesthesia is given, the rosary will not slip out of his hand.
All this Binoy told me afterwards, and without any issue, Mother received the angioplasty from Jesus and gave it back to us safely.
After that, the next problem was the fluid in his lungs; according to the treatment system there, we were not getting any medicine for it.
Because of the fluid in the lungs, Binoy had to sleep sitting up; he could not lie down because he would immediately start gasping and no medicine was available.
At that time I remembered something—earlier I told you I didn’t have faith in Kreupasanam, but about four or five years ago Binoy had come here alone, and— when he came,
he had bought a bottle of honey, which I had kept somewhere among things that were not needed.
I had kept it aside, and I felt Mother telling me, “Daughter, there is some honey kept there, go and check,” so I went and took that honey.
Then every day I prayed, applied the Holy oil, gave that honey, and said, “Mother, we have no other option now; there is fluid in the lungs and we are not getting any treatment here.”
Every day I prayed like that, and along with it I did one more thing—I started prayers properly; I began listening to the Covenant meditations and Father’s talks.
I also started listening to testimonies, and the thing that touched me most was the first condition: to forgive those whom we need to forgive.
So I told Jesus, “I do have people I haven’t forgiven; I have people I don’t speak to,” and I prayed that as I forgive people one by one, Binoy should be able to sleep lying down.
I called everyone I could remember and asked forgiveness and prayed.
After that, the fluid in Binoy’s lungs started decreasing, and the Binoy who could only sleep sitting began to sleep lying down.
In this way Mother solved many matters in Binoy’s life through the Holy oil we used.
The wound he had—if you want, I can show you the photo—was very severe and fully infected.
In the early days the nurses would come to our home to dress the wound.
One day, I felt Mother telling me, “Daughter, draw the sign of the cross with the oil and say the Profession of Faith.”
So I said the Profession of Faith over the wound and applied the oil there.
On the very first day I applied the oil, it was snowing heavily outside, and when I looked out, there was a grey-colored dove sitting on the neighbor’s roof.
On that first day of applying the oil, I understood that there is some power in this oil, and from that day onward I continued applying the oil every day.
I gave honey and blessed salt and did many such things, and then one day I realized the Pilgrim Mother’s guidance is not for nothing.
Binoy had to take antibiotics continuously, and one day the expired antibiotics were kept in the fridge by mistake.
The nurse who usually came to dress the wound did not come that day; instead, another nurse came—just for that one day in all six months of visits.
That nurse told me, “Daughter, this medicine has crossed its expiry date,” and truly, if she had not come that day—
I would have continued giving the expired antibiotic to Binoy for another five days.
But even there, Mother intervened and showed it to us, and we threw away all those medicines.
In the same way, I have another testimony to share about our daughter.
She had asthma, and on the day the rosary I received with the homeopathic medicine I brought from here for her.
I had brought the medicine to give her, but I never ended up giving it. From that day onward, I believed, recited the Profession of Faith, and gave her only the honey and blessed salt from here.
And from February—the month we took the Covenant—till today, our daughter has had no asthma or breathing problem at all.
I didn’t even remember that I had placed this matter in the Covenant due to the situation we were in, but Mother completely healed her.
Likewise, Mother herself brought people to our home—three or four of them—with the blessed medals.
In Canada, you cannot come running like here; everything is far and isolated, yet four people brought the blessed medals to us.
They placed them on Binoy’s wounds and lungs and prayed, and the results were many—too many to explain.
We also started a group, and I will say that Mother herself gave me that group.
After listening to Father’s meditations, one day Father said, “From this day onward, something will happen in your life.”
I noted that date in the calendar.
That day I started a group, and every day we pray the Rosary in it.
From May to November, every single month, I have seen a rainbow—I saw a rainbow every month.
And now, about our journey: we never expected that we could come here in December; we never thought it was possible, but Mother planned everything and brought us here even before December 7th.
Another thing we did for Binoy’s healing was something I deeply believe in—the Holy Mass.
When Binoy was very sick I would go for Mass, and one day it came to my mind, “What is wrong if I take Binoy also?” So I started taking him to Holy Mass,
and our priest was a great support for us.
There was heavy snow—really heavy snow—but still I would take Binoy in the wheelchair; he couldn’t wear boots because of the wound, and because of the antibiotic, he couldn’t wear a winter jacket, but still I took him.
Because after taking the Covenant, I understood deeply what the Holy Mass really is, something I never understood earlier.
From that day onward I took Binoy regularly.
Binoy would first sit there, and Father would come and give him Holy Communion; it was our own Malayalam liturgy.
After that I prayed to Mother, “Mother, on Easter day, let Binoy walk and receive the Lord.” Mother fulfilled it—on Easter day,
Binoy himself walked and received Jesus.
After that I prayed to Mother, “Mother, let Binoy read the Bible,” and Mother granted that too.
Then I prayed, “Mother, let Binoy go up to the altar,” and Mother fulfilled that within one month.
When we were leaving on Tuesday, after attending our Malayalam Mass, Binoy climbed into the altar himself in our malayalam Parish before we left.
We knew this journey would be difficult because he was still sick, but Mother brought us here without a single problem.
After coming here, when Binoy went to take the Covenant, earlier he could only climb two or three steps, yet— the place to take the Covenant was on the second floor,
and I saw Binoy walking up very calmly.
For nine months he had only climbed two or three steps in total, yet I saw him go up step by step all the way to the top.
He went up and did everything, and then he came back down with the same steady speed.
After nine months, this was the first time he climbed so many steps, and when he came down I asked him, “This is the first time you climbed so many steps!”
That’s when Binoy remembered and said, “Yes, this is the first time I’ve climbed this many steps.” After that Binoy said,
“Now nothing will happen to me; if I can climb these steps in front of Mother, why should I be afraid of anything? I don’t need to fear anymore.”
We bought the tickets suddenly.
When we bought the ticket I told Mother, “Mother, if it is your wish, let us reach there before the 7th date; otherwise it’s okay.” But I also said,
“Mother, our financial situation is very bad—we haven’t been able to work for so many months.” So I prayed,
“Mother, only if we get the ticket below 2000 dollars can we come; otherwise it is not possible. Tickets are around 2500 dollars because of vacation time.” But Mother gave us tickets for 1800 dollars,
and within a week we booked them and came here.
Yesterday, standing before Mother, we experienced a fragrance anointing; we have a group, and they all long to see Mother.
Yesterday night no one else was here, so we video-called everyone from our group.
As we showed them the place on video, all three of us began experiencing a very beautiful fragrance.
Truly speaking, it was an extraordinary smell.
Also, Friday was when we booked the ticket—let me mention another blessing: after booking the ticket Friday night, on Sunday morning Binoy’s leg had a small bump like a boil.
It was not serious at first, but by Sunday morning it burst again, and we thought our whole journey was going to end there.
We went to the hospital, and they said there was nothing to do, just continue dressing the wound.
But I told Mother, “This won’t work, we have to travel,” and I applied the oil and prayed with faith.
Then I felt Mother telling me, “Daughter, pray by placing the medal,” and I again tell you—this simple medal we have is very powerful.
Because for us living there, getting the actual Covenant medal quickly is not possible, but even this simple medal carries great strength.
So we placed the medal over the wound and prayed on Sunday and Monday, saying, “Mother, we must travel; there is no other option, only your grace.”
When I came home after my duty on Tuesday, I said, “Let me check once,” and we decided to check again the next morning.
But when I removed the dressing that night, the boil-like swelling had burst completely, and I can only say it was a miracle of Mother.
In Canada, Father knows we have a big prayer center run by Brother Suresh.
Father came there last year and led a retreat, and after that retreat a large statue of Mother was placed there.
I’m saying this so that people in Canada who hear my testimony may know.
When Father came, the statue was installed, and in May I went there; I went with a broken heart.
When I looked, I expected a small statue, but it was a very big statue, and I sat under it crying for three to four hours.
Then I understood Mother was sitting there alone, and I told her, “Mother, I will bring people here however I can.”
And within a month we conducted a big Perpetual rosary prayer service there.
I am saying this for the people in Canada—because it is not easy for anyone to come here quickly, but Mother’s presence is very real there.
Brother Suresh Dominic is there, and we prayed the Rosary very beautifully there.
Whoever in Canada is troubled can go there with confidence; everyone is very helpful there, and Mother is truly present.
We fully believe that Mother is with us, and though we cannot do works of mercy like you do here,
through our group we help many people and pray daily for them.
From our income we also give a small portion to help others, and I have one more thing to tell you—about sacrifice.
When we take the Covenant, we are able to make small sacrifices, and I want to tell you the sacrifice we made in our life.
After taking the Covenant, we gradually came to understand many things we can do; since February, there was heavy snow where we lived.
At first my sacrifice was for Binoy’s healing, but later when I went close to Jesus, I understood it was more than that—it had to be for Jesus.
So I began making sacrifices; what I did was sleep on the floor.
I would lay just a mat and a blanket and sleep on the floor; it was very cold, extremely cold outside, but I still slept like that.
I slept like that for four to five months for Jesus.
And many such sacrifices can be made; and I want to say—if we have even a little health, let us go for Holy Mass.
After attending Holy Mass, Jesus truly heals us; I say this because I have complete conviction of it.
When we receive Jesus, He truly comes close to us and heals us.
As for evangelization, I never intended to do anything—I’m not someone who takes newsletters and distributes them.
But Mother placed two or three bundles of papers into my hands whenever someone came from here, and I have been able to give those papers to whomever needed them.
I give those papers to people there, and in such a short time we have received so many blessings of the Mother of Kreupasanam from Jesus.
For all these blessings Jesus, God, and the Holy Spirit have given us through Mother Mary, we give abundant thanks.
I want to say that I had given up social media because I was a very addicted person—I used to watch movies every day and could not sleep without Facebook.
But for some time now I have had no desire to watch any of it; I left all that behind.
When we make sacrifices for Jesus, Jesus will surely bless us; our problem is that we make our own plans and then tell Jesus, “Lord, give me this, give me that.”
That is our mistake.
And when we don’t get what we planned, we become sad, but once we surrender to Jesus and say, “Lord, let me live as You desire,” then we will have no sadness.
Whenever new sufferings and problems came again and again as in the case of Binoy,
we began praying like this: “Jesus, if someone receives a blessing because of the suffering we are going through now, that is our greatest joy.”
We tried to turn our sufferings into blessings for others,
and once we began doing that, disappointment left our life; hope came in, joy came in, and great courage came in.
Our problems always look big, but once we surrender them to Jesus and try to live according to His will, our problems become nothing.
Then Jesus will plan everything, and truly speaking, Jesus and Mother planned everything and brought us here.
After all the struggles we faced, we have finally reached here in Mother’s presence; once again we thank Jesus and Mother greatly.
I will let my husband speak now— I wants to thank the Holy Mother who appeared on this altar and our Lord Jesus.
We are extremely happy that our long-time desire—to come here first to thank Mother and Jesus, and then do everything else—has been fulfilled.
Yesterday morning we landed here, and without even going home we came straight from the airport directly to this place.
We are very happy that we could come here and give our testimony; we offer great thanks to Mother and to Lord Jesus.
Ezekiel 36:26–27 — “I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and make you walk according to My statutes, and keep My ordinances faithfully.” Binoy Paul and Nitha Mary,
as a couple, are joyfully and proudly sharing their life testimony here at the shrine of Mother of Kreupasanam.
More than the physical healing her husband received, Nitha has shared with us the spiritual awareness and understanding they gained in life.
From the earlier misunderstandings and lack of faith about Kreupasanam and Mother,
to the days when she began to truly know Mother— the daughter happily shares the great changes that took place in their family and life.
Today she stands at the altar sharing how, as a Marian missionary of Kreupasanam,
she is able to spread Mother’s presence wherever she goes.
Through her words, she tells us the value of the Covenant life.
Even after returning to her homeland after a long time, without meeting relatives or friends, without even visiting her own house,
she spent three days here in Mother’s shrine in prayer and giving testimony.
During these days she also showed Mother to her friends abroad through video calls, praying together with them—these were the beautiful acts she did.
Dear ones, the Covenant life makes us owners of a heart of flesh; it transforms our stone hearts that do not absorb water.
We have heard this through the daughter’s words— what her behavior used to be, what her life used to be, what her interests were,
and how the Holy Spirit transformed her life and her family into a dwelling place for God.
There is only one thing—to examine whether we are living with purity, how deep our repentance is, how sincere our contrition is, and how willing we are to forgive.
When we see the sufferings in others’ lives, are we able to respond with compassion through our own life?
These are truly the measuring scales of the Covenant life.
The sister said, “Each time I forgave someone, it helped my husband sleep peacefully even in the midst of a severe illness.
Each time I prayed the rosary, my husband grew calm and received healing.
As our sufferings increased, seeing others receive blessings through them became our greatest joy.
Not even once did we live disappointed about our lacks, our sickness, or our brokenness.” When doctors said her husband’s leg must be amputated,
from that hopeless situation they traveled all this way, climbed these stairs, took the Covenant, and now their son stands here giving testimony.
Dear ones, every word shared here is a life experience of those who rise up by trusting in God.
Do we not say, “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength; they will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not faint”?
The setbacks we face in life are not our strength, but the refuge we find in God is our strength—this is what the daughter shares at this altar.
Our problem is that we keep giving God our lists, yet we fail to hear what God is telling us.
When we embrace the spirit of the Covenant—“Let God’s will be done”—
we are able to face even the greatest problems of life with peace and self-control and move forward.
Illnesses will fade away, financial stability will come, family relationships will be restored, and opportunities will arise to do the good we desire to do.
For the great protection Mother and Jesus gave this family during these days— for the healing of the life partner,
for strengthening the spiritual life of the family, and for opening paths to help many others— let us thank Mother and the Holy Son with a round of applause as we offer this testimony.
